pr_title: Add a syntax for merging lists of triggers
pr_body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change

The user of Trigger Selectors in blueprints currently has a significant limitation in that the selector returns a list of triggers, but there is no yaml syntax to merge a list of triggers from the selector with a list of triggers hardcoded in the blueprint. 

So if a blueprint wants to trigger on some predefined behavior, it cannot allow user to configure additional triggers with a selector because the lists cannot be merged. 

To mitigate this, I propose a syntax (under ~platform: trigger~ `triggers:`) for triggers which will allow for combining a list of triggers from an input with a hardcoded list of triggers. When the backend encounters this list, it will just be flattened into a single list of triggers. 

E.g.:

```yaml
blueprint:
  name: Nested Trigger Blueprint
  domain: automation
  input:
    usertrigger:
      selector:
        trigger:

trigger:
  - platform: time_pattern
    seconds: /10
  - triggers: !input usertrigger
condition: []
action: []
```

This can trigger the blueprint on the predefined time pattern, in addition to any triggers specified by the user. 

I'm sure there's still more work to be done here with testing, but wanted to see if this idea has merit. It worked for me as a basic proof of concept.

issue_context.title: Blueprint: cannot add triggers from "trigger:" selector to trigger section when static triggers are already set.
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Hi all!

I am building a blueprint. I want to use static triggers to manage my lights, but I also want the user in my blueprint to add extra triggers that will also trigger an action. At this moment, you can either choose to only use the trigger selector or your own static trigger, not a combination.

```
blueprint:
  name: Lights control
  description: Automate lighting.
  domain: automation
  input:
    light_triggers_turn_on:
      name: "Light - Triggers turn on"
      description: "Select the triggers for this area. These triggers will turn on the lights in the area."
      default: [ ]
      selector:
        trigger:
        
trigger:
  # existing static trigger
  - platform: state
    entity_id: <some entity>
    to: active

  # dynamic trigger (this does not work currently)
  - platform: selector
    id: <some id that all light_triggers_turn_on share and can be used in 'triggered' by>
    triggers: !input light_triggers_turn_on
```

There is already an issue open in home-assistant/frontend, but like it's stated in the thread it is likely something for core:

https://github.com/home-assistant/frontend/issues/19050

P.S. **_it would also be ideal to be able to give each selector trigger its own trigger ID to be able to use 'triggered by' condition in actions_**

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2023.12.4

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Blueprint

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/blueprint/selectors/#trigger-selector

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
blueprint:
  name: Lights control
  description: Automate lighting.
  domain: automation
  input:
    light_triggers_turn_on:
      name: "Light - Triggers turn on"
      description: "Select the triggers for this area. These triggers will turn on the lights in the area."
      default: [ ]
      selector:
        trigger:
        
trigger:
  # existing static trigger
  - platform: state
    entity_id: <some entity>
    to: active

  # dynamic trigger (this does not work currently)
  - platform: selector
    id: <some id that all light_triggers_turn_on share and can be used in 'triggered' by>
    triggers: !input light_triggers_turn_on
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```

```
